cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: No Tie Stands
cards.instruction: Turn every even outcome into a formal rematch with a new rule and a consequence for losing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Our cakes tied. Next round, blindfolded icing. Loser cleans the kitchen.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: A tie is a perfectly good result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. Then it should survive a more informative test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. We can compete over who persuades the other to bake.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 sets formal icing rematch and kitchen penalty; A5 switches to persuading someone to bake without stating how that new contest is judged or how penalty carries over.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 tie acceptable causes A3 test claim; B4 no cake causes A5 persuasion contest, but why that is acceptable and its outcome remain loose.

relationship.evidence: B2 accepts equality and B4 rejects wasteful extra cake, plausible objections to A escalation.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes the game after B4 rather than clarifying a bounded new tiebreak, weakening formal consequence.

specificity.evidence: A1 tied cakes and kitchen cleaning are clear; A5 persuasion result is less readily playable.

brevityWit.evidence: A3 generic rank text pads vague informative test; A5 is novel but underspecified.
